checkIns.result: Found and fixed a REAL correctness bug this cycle. healthcheck:legacy was GREEN (A/B/C/D as expected) but C_record's own resolved count caught my eye: 30 (23:51 UTC cycle) -> 26 (00:07 UTC cycle) within ~16 minutes with zero market activity in between (Friday evening, RTH long closed). Root-caused to fetchNighthawkOutcomeAnalytics/fetchNighthawkFunnelStats (src/lib/db.ts) windowing their edition_for cutoff off bare Postgres CURRENT_DATE, which resolves in the DB session's UTC timezone -- edition_for is an ET trading-day date, so between ~8pm and midnight ET (exactly the window we're in), CURRENT_DATE has already ticked to the next UTC day and the 14-day window's cutoff lands a day later than intended, prematurely dropping the oldest ET trading day. db.ts already has the identical fix pattern elsewhere (flow-alerts DTE query, '(NOW() AT TIME ZONE America/New_York)::date', with a comment explicitly calling out this exact 8pm-midnight ET failure mode) -- it just was never applied to these two Night Hawk functions. Fixed all 3 call sites (1 in fetchNighthawkOutcomeAnalytics, 2 in fetchNighthawkFunnelStats), added 2 new source-inspection regression tests in db.test.ts (DB integration testing unavailable in this sandbox) proving RED against the pre-fix CURRENT_DATE clauses then GREEN after, tsc --noEmit clean, full local suite kicked off in background (large suite, still running at PR-open time). Opened PR #4816 as draft, subscribed to its activity, staged finding docs/audit/findings-staging/2026-09-12-nighthawk-record-window-utc-anchor.md, added a MARKET-OPEN-VALIDATION.md watch-list entry. This is a real member-visible correctness bug: win_rate_pct/resolved/segments on /record silently shift with zero underlying data change for several hours every trading evening. Impact scope confirmed Legacy-only (fetchNighthawkOutcomeAnalytics/fetchNighthawkFunnelStats have no other callers; 0DTE/Swings use separate tables).

checkIns.note: Real design/correctness finding while reviewing technicals.ts: swingLevels() sorts its detected 45-session pivot highs/lows by raw MAGNITUDE (dedup() sorts ascending by value, then .slice(-5)/.slice(0,5) picks the top/bottom 5) rather than by distance to current spot. This means support_levels[0] is always the single LOWEST support pivot in the lookback window and resistance_levels[0] is always the single HIGHEST resistance pivot -- the FARTHEST level from price among everything detected, not the nearest. Both direct consumers read index [0] with no re-sort in between: deterministic-edition.ts's resolveLevels() (firstFinite(tech?.support_levels)/firstFinite(tech?.resistance_levels), lines 334-335 -- the CORE synthesis path for every deterministically-generated Legacy play) and play-backfill.ts's thin-edition rescue (dossier.tech?.support_levels?.[0]/resistance_levels?.[0], lines 132-133). Traced why this hasn't shown up as a target_unreachable/band_detached publish-gate failure: play-levels.ts's buildDirectionalStockLevels() clamps the resulting stop/target distance to a volatility-scaled max cap (and floors a too-close target, the documented PR-N21/N22 fix) on BOTH sides, so the final published number lands in a sensible ATR-scaled band regardless of whether the seed level was near or far -- an unrelated safety clamp absorbs the bug's numeric consequences. What doesn't get absorbed: when the farthest-pivot value happens to already sit inside that clamp band (common for a moderately volatile name), it's used as-is, so the play's stop/target is anchored to -- and any level-context text cites -- the LEAST relevant technical level available rather than the nearest one. A picks-quality/narrative-honesty issue, not a geometry-safety one, but it touches the core level-selection logic for every Legacy play. Confirmed zero test coverage of swingLevels()'s ordering semantics exists (technicals.test.ts only covers classifySetup/buildTechnicalSummary) -- this reads as an oversight, not a verified deliberate design choice. PROOF (direct from source, no live repro needed): a target_unreachable BLOCK only ever enters result.blocks[] when targetAtrMultiple > GATE_TARGET_MAX_ATR_MULTIPLE (evaluateNighthawkPublishGates line 223: targetOk = targetAtrMultiple <= GATE_TARGET_MAX_ATR_MULTIPLE; blocks.push(...) only when !targetOk). isPromotableBlockedPlay (line 392) rejects that SAME block's value when v > GATE_PROMOTE_TARGET_MAX_ATR_MULTIPLE. Since both constants equal 2.0, 'targetAtrMultiple > 2.0' (necessary for the block to exist at all) ALWAYS implies 'v > 2.0' (necessary for promote-rejection) -- the two conditions are identical, so every real target_unreachable block is unconditionally non-promotable. There is no value of targetAtrMultiple for which a target_unreachable-blocked play can ever be rescued.

Why this matters: target_unreachable is the ONE gate code this file deliberately excludes from NON_PROMOTABLE_GATE_CODES, with an extensive comment explaining exactly why -- 'blocking rescue on this gate is what caused the Jul 27 zero-play edition (all 5 plays blocked, zero promotable, recap-only published)'. The comment on GATE_TARGET_MAX_ATR_MULTIPLE itself says 'Gate-promote rescue caps even lower (GATE_PROMOTE_TARGET_MAX_ATR_MULTIPLE) so thin editions cannot resurrect unreachable targets' -- language that only makes sense if the promote cap sits ABOVE the hard gate (giving genuine rescue room between them), not equal to it. As shipped, the exclusion from NON_PROMOTABLE_GATE_CODES is dead: the SAME zero-play-edition failure mode this mechanism exists to prevent can still occur today if every blocked play in a thin edition happens to fail ONLY on target_unreachable.

Test-suite corroboration: publish-gates.test.ts:555 ('promoteTopBlocked promotes target_unreachable only when multiple <= rescue cap') asserts isPromotableBlockedPlay returns true for a synthetic block with value:1.8, threshold:2.0 -- but value:1.8 is LESS than GATE_TARGET_MAX_ATR_MULTIPLE (2.0), meaning this exact block could never actually be produced by evaluateNighthawkPublishGates in the first place (a target_unreachable block only exists when its value EXCEEDS 2.0). The test passes today, but only because it feeds isPromotableBlockedPlay an artificial value the real gate evaluator can never produce -- it gives false confidence that the rescue path works when wired end-to-end, it doesn't.
checkIns.whyReportNotFix: The correct fix needs a NEW, genuinely higher value for GATE_PROMOTE_TARGET_MAX_ATR_MULTIPLE (something strictly between 2.0 and infinity, giving real rescue headroom) -- this is a product/risk calibration decision (how much beyond the hard gate should the platform be willing to auto-promote when an edition would otherwise publish empty), not something derivable from existing code/tests/patterns the way the trough-floor or crossed-book-mark fixes earlier this session were (those mirrored an ALREADY-ESTABLISHED sibling pattern; this one requires inventing a new number). The file's own history (the base gate was tightened from a documented OLD value of 3.5x down to today's 2.0x, per GATE_TARGET_MAX_ATR_MULTIPLE's own comment) suggests 3.0-3.5x as a plausible candidate ceiling, but picking the actual number is an operator/Cursor call, not mine to make unilaterally on live picks-publishing logic. Per CARVE-OUT: ambiguous/live-picks-logic -> report, hold.
checkIns.nextStep: Whoever picks this up: (1) choose GATE_PROMOTE_TARGET_MAX_ATR_MULTIPLE's correct value (candidate: something in [2.5, 3.5] range, ideally re-derived from the same touch-rate measurement target-reachability.ts already documents using, e.g. the historical rate at 2.5x/3.0x), (2) fix publish-gates.test.ts:561's synthetic fixture to use a value that could actually be produced by the real gate (something >2.0 but <= the new promote cap, e.g. 2.5 if the cap becomes 3.0), (3) add a NEW test that feeds a target_unreachable block through BOTH evaluateNighthawkPublishGates AND isPromotableBlockedPlay end-to-end (not isPromotableBlockedPlay alone with a hand-built fixture) to catch this exact composition gap if it recurs.

reportAndHold.title: Published play RANK is sorted by raw score, but member-facing CONVICTION is assigned later by a deliberately NON-monotonic tier engine -- rank and conviction can (and tonight DO) disagree, so the '#1' play is not the highest-conviction one
reportAndHold.evidence: edition-builder.ts:1144-1149 (PR-N26): `finalPlays.sort((a,b) => (b.score ?? -Infinity) - (a.score ?? -Infinity))` with the comment 're-rank by score descending so the highest-conviction play is always #1'. But `conviction` is NOT set at this point in the pipeline -- it is derived later, per-request, by edition-outcome-overlay.ts reading the tier pinned by publish-context.ts's assignNighthawkTier (nighthawk-tiers.ts, PR-N7), which is DELIBERATELY non-monotonic in score by design: the tier engine's own header comment documents the measured overnight track record showing the 40-55 'prime' score band outperforming the 70+ 'top' band (avg +2.99% vs -0.55%/0-for-1), so a LOWER score can legitimately earn a HIGHER tier letter. VERIFIED LIVE against tonight's edition (GET /api/market/nighthawk/edition, 2026-09-16 23:2x UTC): SMTC rank=1 score=78 conviction=B; LITE rank=2 score=71 conviction=B; RVTY rank=3 score=53 conviction=A. RVTY is tonight's ONLY A-conviction play and it is ranked LAST, exactly inverted from the sort's own stated purpose. This is not a hypothetical -- it is the actual state of the edition members are looking at right now.
reportAndHold.whyNotCarveOut: This is live-picks display-order logic (which play members see presented as the '#1'/top pick), not a safe, contained correctness fix -- exactly the ESCALATION category CLAUDE.md carves out from unilateral fixing ('Ambiguous/live-picks-logic -> report, hold'). A fix requires computing each play's tier BEFORE this sort (the tier engine is pure and callable here -- dossiers[ticker].scored is already in scope, same nhTierInputFromScored input publish-context.ts uses downstream) and choosing a sort key (tier rank first, score as tiebreaker within a tier) plus deciding whether existing published editions' historical rank fields should be considered affected. That is a real design decision about how the product presents conviction, not a one-line bug fix, and it changes what members see as the lead pick on every future edition -- worth operator/Cursor visibility before touching.
reportAndHold.candidateFixSketch: At the same point ranked/dossiers are still in scope (before line 1144), compute `assignNighthawkTier(nhTierInputFromScored(dossiers[play.ticker].scored))` per finalPlay (mirrors publish-context.ts:266-272 exactly, so it can't drift from the pin), sort by tier rank descending (A > B > C, matching NH_TIER_RANK in nighthawk-tiers.ts) with score as the tiebreaker within a tier, THEN assign rank. gate_promoted plays already get capGatePromotedConviction applied at the read-time overlay, so their sort-time tier should probably also route through that cap for consistency -- worth deciding explicitly rather than assuming either way.

correctionToPriorFinding.headline: MATERIAL CORRECTION + SEVERITY UPGRADE on the open rank-vs-conviction finding: the raw-score ordering isn't just a display bug -- it can affect WHICH plays get published at all, not just their displayed order.
correctionToPriorFinding.detail: Traced deterministic-edition.ts's buildDeterministicEditionPlays (the source of the plays list critiquePlays receives) to find where its output order actually comes from. Line 897-906: right after the build loop finishes, grounded+skipGrounding plays are MERGED and SORTED by raw governor-adjusted score (`scoreMap.get(ticker) ?? score`) -- this is a SEPARATE, EARLIER raw-score sort than the PR-N26 one in edition-builder.ts flagged two cycles ago. This corrects my prior framing (that the pre-PR-N26 order was still tier-aware from rankCandidates) -- it is NOT; the tier-aware order from rankCandidates only governs the BUILD LOOP's selection eligibility order (which candidates get attempted first), not the final list order, which is raw-score-sorted here already, one stage before critic and two stages before edition-builder.ts's own redundant re-sort. MORE IMPORTANTLY (line 917): `let finalPlays = merged.slice(0, target)` -- the raw-score-sorted list is SLICED to the target play count (`buffer = target + 20` means up to 20 more candidates than the target can be built and grounded before this cutoff). This means the raw-score ordering doesn't just misorder the final displayed rank -- it determines WHICH candidates survive into the published edition at all whenever more candidates clear the build loop than the target slot count. A genuinely higher-tier (measured-better-performing, per the tier engine's own evidence) but lower-raw-score candidate can be CUT here in favor of a higher-raw-score, lower-tier one -- before conviction is even assigned, before the critic runs, before PR-N26's redundant final sort. This is a SELECTION defect, not merely a presentation one.
correctionToPriorFinding.severityChange: Upgrades this from 'members see a lower-conviction play labeled #1' to 'a genuinely better-tiered play can be silently excluded from the published edition entirely, replaced by a worse-tiered higher-score one, whenever candidate volume exceeds the target play count.' Still REPORT AND HOLD -- this is now clearly a scope question (does the fix belong at the deterministic-edition.ts merge-sort, the edition-builder.ts final sort, or both -- and unlike a pure display reorder, changing the SELECTION cutoff changes which tickers members actually see picks for on a given night) squarely inside the 'ambiguous/live-picks-logic' escalation category, not a shrinking-risk simplification anymore. Flagging the severity upgrade explicitly so a reviewing session/operator/Cursor does not under-prioritize this against the more cosmetic framing from two cycles ago.

knownOpenItems.legacyCalendarTileNullPremiumAsZero_2026:
Live finding, 2026-09-15 ~14:37 UTC: today's calendar day-tile (SEP 15) reads '+0%' even though VNCE (the day's only play) is up ~+10-12% stock move and near its target -- because VNCE is stock-only (no options data), its premiumPct is genuinely null (fail-closed, by design -- see use-legacy-quotes.ts's own MU-$880C comment), but legacyBoardCalendarBuckets (legacy-board-table-utils.ts:174-206) computes 'net = resolved.reduce((s,r) => s + (r.premiumPct ?? 0), 0)' then 'net_premium_pct: resolved.length ? Math.round(net / resolved.length) : 0' -- the ?? 0 coalesce means a null premiumPct (no data) is indistinguishable from an actually-measured 0% return in the divisor/numerator, so a day whose only play(s) are all stock-only silently reads as 'flat' rather than 'no premium data yet'. This is exactly the absence-read-as-presence trap this codebase's own audit discipline (LARGO-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md's absence principle, the pulled-play net_premium fix already in this same function's comment) exists to prevent -- and it's a real, reproducible, current-day live instance, not a hypothetical. NOT shipped as a fix -- the clean fix (excluding null-premiumPct rows from the averaging denominator, and representing 'zero real data points' distinctly from 'measured zero') needs the bucket to carry a has_data flag or a nullable net_premium_pct, and VectorBoardCalendarBucket / fmtSigned (VectorBoardCalendar.tsx) are SHARED across other lanes' boards (0DTE/Swings also use vector-board-table-utils.ts's family of types) -- outside Legacy's ownership boundary per the standing mandate ('Not yours: 0DTE or Swings'). Flagging for operator/Cursor review rather than touching a shared type unilaterally. Candidate fix direction (not decided): legacyBoardCalendarBuckets could compute its own Legacy-local 'has real premium data' flag without changing the shared type's shape, if the render layer can be taught to treat a specific sentinel (e.g. n>0 but winners+closed+0-net all zero) as ambiguous -- needs a real design decision either way, not a mechanical patch.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-15 (new-hour :06 cycle): investigated the shared vector-board-row-utils.ts 'AVG GIVEBACK' stat (rendered as an honest '--' on today's board) as a fresh angle, and found strong reinforcing evidence for the recommended fix direction here. vectorBoardScorecard (SAME file) already computes netPremiumPct, hitRate, winnersFloorPct, runnerPipelinePct, AND avgGivebackPct ALL with the exact 'null when no real data, never a fabricated 0' pattern -- each uses its own counted-denominator variable (pctN/hitDenom/openTotal/givebackN) incremented only on real values, and returns `null` (not 0) when that counter is 0. So the eventual fix for legacyBoardCalendarBuckets's net_premium_pct (making it nullable, '--' in the UI for a genuinely-no-premium-data day) would not be a novel design choice -- it would be copying an already-dominant, four-times-repeated pattern in this exact file. This doesn't change the scope call (still a shared VectorBoardCalendarBucket type change, still outside Legacy's ownership boundary, still not shipped this session) but makes the case for whoever picks it up much stronger and lower-risk than a from-scratch design decision would be.

Confirmed the SAME root pattern (stock-only plays invisible to premium-gated aggregates) extends well beyond the calendar tile: today's scorecard header reads '0 picks... 0 winners, 0 runners... Hit rate 0%', WINNERS FLOOR shows 'Open winners 0%', RUNNER PIPELINE shows 'Open runners 0%' -- ALL despite VNCE being a real, currently-winning stock move 93% of the way to its target.
